citations.S1: SQL injection — critical.** `user_id` and `status` come straight from the HTTP request and are interpolated into the query
citations.S2: Connection/cursor never closed — medium.** `conn`/`cur` are never closed
citations.S3: `order[0]` is the integer `id` column; `"Order #" + order[0]` raises `TypeError: can only concatenate str`
citations.S4: Division by zero in `average_order_value` — high.** Empty `orders` list → `ZeroDivisionError`
citations.S5: Money represented as float — high (data integrity).** `amount` is summed/divided/discounted as a float throughout
citations.S6: A negative `pct` increases the price; `pct > 100` produces a negative amount
citations.S7: There's no allowlist for known status values
citations.S8: Missing authorization (IDOR) — critical.** The function trusts `user_id` from the request
citations.S9: If a row ever has a non-numeric `amount` (bad data, schema drift), this throws a `TypeError`
citations.S11: likely surfacing a raw traceback (and potentially schema/path details) to the client. Fix: catch `sqlite3.Error`, log it with context, raise/return a sanitized error
citations.S12: No rounding policy on the discounted amount — medium.** ... Fix: round once, at the boundary, with an explicit policy (e.g. `ROUND_HALF_UP` to 2 decimal places)
citations.S13: Unbounded result set — low.** No `LIMIT`/pagination on the orders query
